_comment: Importable Orcabot dashboard template. Unlike the other benchmark templates this one needs no orchestrator, no agent and no API key: the terminal's boot command runs the whole benchmark and serves its report on localhost, and the browser block is pointed at that server. Seed with bin/seed-benchmark-templates.
name: TTS Benchmark Runner
description: Run the open-weight TTS benchmark and read its report

items.content:
{"name": "TTS benchmark", "agentic": false, "bootCommand": "MODELS=piper PORT=8099 # talkito refuses to fetch model weights when it cannot ask a human, and a boot # command has no TTY. Without this every phrase fails with "Piper model # unavailable" while the run still exits 0 and publishes an empty table. export TALKITO_AUTO_APPROVE_DOWNLOADS=1 ROOT=/workspace/talkito BENCH=$ROOT/benchmark SERVE=/workspace/tts-report echo "== Orcabot: talkito TTS benchmark ($MODELS) ==" # Serve a placeholder first, so the browser block has something at a stable URL from # the first second rather than an error until the run finishes. mkdir -p "$SERVE" [ -f "$SERVE/index.html" ] || printf '%s' 'TTS benchmark

Benchmark running...

This page reloads every 10 seconds. The report replaces it when the run finishes.

' > "$SERVE/index.html" curl -sf -o /dev/null --max-time 2 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" || ( cd "$SERVE" && nohup python3 -m http.server "$PORT" >/workspace/.tts-serve.log 2>&1 & ) # talkito's .gitmodules uses git@github.com: URLs and the sandbox has no SSH key, # so --recurse-submodules fails; both repos are cloned over HTTPS instead. # The harness now ships inside talkito-benchmark, so tests-repo is not needed -- # but tools/paths.py still wants a talkito CHECKOUT (it looks for talkito/tts.py, # not the installed package), and benchmark/ inside talkito/ is the layout it # resolves via "../..". [ -d "$ROOT/.git" ] || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/robdmac/talkito.git "$ROOT" [ -d "$BENCH/.git" ] || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/robdmac/talkito-benchmark.git "$BENCH" # make_samples.py shells out to ffmpeg to turn the listening clip into an mp3, and # the sandbox image ships without it. Missing, the sweep still scores normally and # only the play button is lost, so this is a soft dependency -- but a table of # numbers with nothing to hear is most of the point of the page. command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 || { apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends ffmpeg; } # piper needs no torch at all, and faster-whisper scores on CPU through CTranslate2, # so the whole piper arm installs in seconds. Heavier models would need much more. python3 -c 'import piper' 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --break-system-packages -q piper-tts python3 -c 'import faster_whisper' 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --break-system-packages -q faster-whisper cd "$BENCH" || exec bash # The listening clip has to exist before the page is built, or the table is numbers # with nothing to play. benchmark.py builds the page at the end, so samples come first. python3 tools/make_samples.py $(echo "$MODELS" | tr , ' ') # build_benchmark_page.py defaults TTS_SAMPLE_DIR to a hardcoded # /Users/robertmacrae/... path, so off that one machine it finds no clips and # builds a table with nothing to play. make_samples.py resolves the same variable # with expanduser and writes its mp3s to a "mp3" subdirectory, so the two only # agree when the variable is set explicitly -- and they want different values, # which is why this is set here rather than once at the top. # --only skips the interactive picker, which needs a TTY it does not have here. TTS_SAMPLE_DIR=$HOME/.cache/talkito/benchmark-samples/mp3 python3 tools/benchmark.py --only "$MODELS" rc=$? if [ -f tts-benchmark.html ]; then cp -f tts-benchmark.html "$SERVE/index.html" echo "report published -> http://localhost:$PORT/" else echo "no tts-benchmark.html was produced; measurements (if any) are under $BENCH/tools/" fi echo "[tts benchmark done rc=$rc]" exec bash", "subagentIds": [], "skillIds": [], "mcpToolIds": []}

setupGuide:
# talkito TTS benchmark

This template runs the open-weight TTS benchmark from
[talkito-benchmark](https://github.com/robdmac/talkito-benchmark) end to end inside
one terminal, and shows the report it produces in the browser block beside it.

Unlike the other benchmark templates there is **no orchestrator**. Nothing here needs
Orcabot chat, an agent, or an API key: the terminal's boot command is the whole run,
and the browser block is pointed at a local web server the same command starts. Start
the dashboard and it goes.

## What the terminal does

1. Serves a placeholder page on `localhost:8099`, so the browser block has a stable
   URL immediately instead of an error until the run finishes.
2. Clones `talkito` and `talkito-benchmark` over **HTTPS**. talkito's `.gitmodules`
   uses `git@github.com:` URLs, which cannot work in the sandbox (no SSH key), so
   `--recurse-submodules` is deliberately not used. The harness ships inside
   talkito-benchmark now, so `tests-repo` is not needed -- but `tools/paths.py` still
   wants a talkito *checkout* rather than the installed package (it looks for
   `talkito/tts.py`), and `benchmark/` inside `talkito/` is the layout it resolves.
3. Installs `piper-tts` and `faster-whisper`. Piper uses no torch at all and
   faster-whisper scores on CPU via CTranslate2, so this arm is small and quick.
4. Synthesizes the one listening clip per model (`make_samples.py`) **before** the
   sweep, because `benchmark.py` builds the page at the end and a sample produced
   afterwards would not be in it.
5. Runs `python3 tools/benchmark.py --only piper`, which sweeps the 84-phrase corpus,
   transcribes each clip back with Whisper, scores word error rate, then rebuilds the
   page and the export zip.
6. Copies `tts-benchmark.html` over the placeholder, so the browser block shows the
   report on its next refresh.

## Running more models

`MODELS` on the first line of the boot command is the only thing to change. It is
passed to `--only`, so it is comma-separated:

    MODELS=piper              # the default: minutes
    MODELS=piper,kokoro       # kokoro pulls torch, so expect a long first run
    MODELS=piper,kittentts

There are 73 providers. A **full sweep is around 11 hours** and much longer on a
first run, because every engine downloads its own weights -- which is why this
template ships pinned to piper rather than to everything.

## Reading the result

The report is the same page the published benchmark is built from: one row per
configuration, with word error rate, real-time factor, compute per phrase, PESQ and a
play button per row. `tts-benchmark-export.zip` beside it is the shareable archive
(page + measurements + audio).

Measurements are saved per unit as they complete, so an interrupted run keeps its
finished work and re-running resumes rather than restarting. `--keep` adds to existing
measurements instead of replacing them.

## If the run stops early

The terminal drops to a shell either way and prints `[tts benchmark done rc=N]`.
`rc` is `benchmark.py`'s exit code -- non-zero means at least one provider failed, and
the per-provider output above it says which. The page and the zip can always be
rebuilt from stored measurements alone:

    cd /workspace/talkito/benchmark
    python3 tools/build_benchmark_page.py tts-benchmark.html
